## Survivors (full card fields)

### G01-A1 `TOM_PARTICIPATION`

- **Mechanism:** Recurring fiat-rail cash flows (salary-linked purchases, monthly DCA plans, fund subscriptions and month-end marks) concentrate around the turn of the month, so participation rises on the first days of a month.
- **Exact claim:** Mean over calendar months of [mean z(log daily trade count) over turn-of-month days minus mean z over days 8-21 of the same month] is positive and at least 0.5 comparator-SD, Holm-adjusted two-sided sign-flip p <= 0.05 within TF-G01-A.
- **Inference class:** CONTEXT_DESCRIPTIVE / UNCONDITIONAL / ATOMIC; sign-flip over month units
- **Unit:** calendar month
- **Exposure:** turn-of-month days: the last UTC calendar day of the previous month and days 1-3; minus the last-Friday expiry day and the fixed holiday windows Dec 24-Jan 2 and Oct 1-7
- **Outcome:** log of the UTC-day trade count (Binance 1m `count`; BitMEX 5m `trades`), standardized per year and weekday class (Mon-Fri / Sat-Sun), label-blind
- **Comparator:** days 8-21 of the same month outside the holiday windows
- **Expected nominal n:** about 60 discovery months, 36 replication months; about 3-4 state and 14 comparator days per month
- **Dependence:** months are time-separated; slow participation regimes cancel inside a month; residual serial dependence across months is checked with a moving-block SE
- **Practical bar:** 0.5 comparator-SD (the same product-relevance bar as R03: a shift that roughly doubles the rate of extreme-day flags)
- **Product relevance:** activity ranks and baselines in the briefing; a turn-of-month shift would mis-calibrate a 30-day activity baseline
- **Why not duplicate:** No prior card tests the day-of-month cash-flow clock; turn-of-month appears in no ledger, memory or generator record.
- **Red team:** Lookahead: none (calendar). Hidden conditioning: none. Overlap: state day -1 belongs to the next month's unit only. Pseudo-replication: month units. Multiplicity: Holm within card. Epoch: calendar years, gate per contract. Venue artifact: trade count changes with fragmentation, absorbed by per-year standardization. Exposed-outcome leakage: no day-of-month statistic was ever reported. Survives.
- **Data:** CORE_BTC_BINANCE_V0 (1m, 2020-01..2024-12); D2_BITMEX_PRE2020_XBTUSD (5m, 2017-01..2019-12, replication)
- **Confounders:** weekday composition of state days (removed by weekday-class standardization); monthly expiry on the last Friday (that day is excluded); year-end and CN Golden Week holidays (fixed-date exclusions); floating holidays (CN New Year, US Labor Day) remain as noise
- **Prior overlap:** R03-A2 last-Friday expiry hour (different clock; that day excluded); R03-C weekday/session clock (weekday handled by standardization); GV0V03L40-C028 tax-year-end panel turnover (December only, panel, losers)

### G01-A2 `TOM_RANGE`

- **Mechanism:** If turn-of-month flows are directional and lumpy, they move price more on those days than mid-month, widening the daily range.
- **Exact claim:** As G01-A1 with target z(log daily range ln(max high / min low)).
- **Inference class:** CONTEXT_DESCRIPTIVE / UNCONDITIONAL / ATOMIC; sign-flip over month units
- **Unit:** calendar month
- **Exposure:** as G01-A1
- **Outcome:** log daily range over the UTC day, standardized per year and weekday class
- **Comparator:** as G01-A1
- **Expected nominal n:** as G01-A1
- **Dependence:** as G01-A1
- **Practical bar:** 0.5 comparator-SD
- **Product relevance:** range ranks behind the unusual-hour and daily context
- **Why not duplicate:** as G01-A1
- **Red team:** As G01-A1. The range target is the product-facing one; the participation target is the direct mechanism observable. Both are kept as separate cells (Holm m <= 3). Survives.
- **Data:** CORE_BTC_BINANCE_V0; D2_BITMEX_PRE2020_XBTUSD (replication)
- **Confounders:** as G01-A1; volatility regime (nuisance diagnostic: prior 24h RV, lagged target)
- **Prior overlap:** as G01-A1

### G01-A3 `MONTH_END_MARK_HOUR`

- **Mechanism:** Crypto funds and treasuries mark month-end NAV at 00:00 UTC; rebalancing and marking trades concentrate in the last UTC hour of the month.
- **Exact claim:** Mean over months of [z(log range of 23:00-24:00 UTC on the last day of the month) minus mean z of the same hour on days 8-21] is positive and at least 0.5 SD, Holm within TF-G01-A.
- **Inference class:** CONTEXT_DESCRIPTIVE / UNCONDITIONAL / ATOMIC; sign-flip over month units
- **Unit:** calendar month
- **Exposure:** 23:00-24:00 UTC on the last day of the month (December excluded by the year-end window)
- **Outcome:** log range of the hour, standardized per year and weekday class over all days' 23:00 hours
- **Comparator:** 23:00-24:00 UTC on days 8-21 of the same month
- **Expected nominal n:** about 55 months with one state hour each
- **Dependence:** time-separated months
- **Practical bar:** 0.5 comparator-SD
- **Product relevance:** the unusual-hour flag at the month boundary
- **Why not duplicate:** Different clock (month-end mark, not expiry). Kept so that the compiler, not the author, decides its power.
- **Red team:** Rare-event N is the expected failure; it is sent to the compiler rather than closed by the author, because the R03 precedent is a compiler decision. Survives to feasibility.
- **Data:** CORE_BTC_BINANCE_V0; D2_BITMEX_PRE2020_XBTUSD (replication)
- **Confounders:** one state hour per unit: rare-event power is the expected failure; daily 00:00 UTC funding and candle close affect state and comparator alike
- **Prior overlap:** R03-A2/A3 (monthly single-hour cells closed INFORMATIONALLY_WEAK at feasibility)

### G01-B1 `ETF_FIXING_HOUR_PARTICIPATION`

- **Mechanism:** US spot bitcoin ETFs (trading from 2024-01-11) strike NAV on reference rates computed over 15:00-16:00 New York. Authorized-participant and market-maker execution and the associated CME basis activity concentrate in that window on NYSE trading days, raising its participation relative to the adjacent afternoon hours.
- **Exact claim:** Difference-in-differences over ISO weeks: mean over post-launch weeks of d_week minus mean over pre-launch weeks of d_week is positive and at least 0.5 comparator-SD, two-sided block-permutation p <= 0.05; d_week = mean over NYSE full trading days of [z(log quote volume 15:00-16:00 NY) - mean z(log quote volume 13:00-14:00, 14:00-15:00 NY)].
- **Inference class:** CONTEXT_DESCRIPTIVE / UNCONDITIONAL / ATOMIC; block permutation of era labels over 4-week blocks
- **Unit:** ISO week (pre: 2020-01-01..2024-01-07; post: 2024-01-15..2024-12-31; launch week 2024-W02 dropped)
- **Exposure:** post-launch NYSE full trading days
- **Outcome:** log quote volume of the fixing hour relative to the two preceding hours, standardized per year on a common scale across the three hours
- **Comparator:** the same relative quantity in pre-launch weeks
- **Expected nominal n:** about 209 pre and 50 post weeks; about 4.8 trading days per week
- **Dependence:** serial dependence across weeks (4-week blocks); the within-day difference removes day-level volatility
- **Practical bar:** 0.5 comparator-SD
- **Product relevance:** same-hour baselines that mix NYSE days, weekends and holidays mis-calibrate the 15:00-16:00 NY hour if it changed with ETFs
- **Why not duplicate:** No prior card uses the ETF launch as a natural experiment; ETF NAV fixing appears in no ledger, memory or generator record.
- **Red team:** Lookahead: none (calendar and launch date are public before T). Confounding: the hour also hosts the equity close and CME daily settle, handled by DiD against pre-launch weeks; ETF-unrelated hour-specific trends cannot be removed and are stated. Replication: no historical ETF era exists; prospective only, against the frozen pre-launch mean. Range target not added, to keep a single primary cell. Survives.
- **Data:** CORE_BTC_BINANCE_V0; NYSE_HOLIDAY_CALENDAR_ARCHIVE_V0
- **Confounders:** US equity close and CME daily settlement also sit at 16:00 NY (present in both eras; DiD); hour-specific trends unrelated to ETFs (not removable; stated as a blocking assumption); single post year: epochs are 2024 quarters
- **Prior overlap:** R03-C4 Friday 15:00-16:00 NY vs Tue-Thu (different comparator and question; null); GV0CAL-C004 CME monthly settlement fixing (blocked on confounding); D12 US-clock anchoring (profile shift at DST; different identification)

## Closed before feasibility (no outcome, no repair)

### G01-X1 `HK_ETF_FIXING_0800UTC` — `CLOSED_AT_RED_TEAM`

- **Mechanism:** Hong Kong spot bitcoin ETFs (from 2024-04-30) strike NAV at 16:00 HKT (08:00 UTC).
- **Claim:** Range or participation of 08:00-09:00 UTC after 2024-04-30 vs before, relative to adjacent hours.
- **Why closed:** Not identifiable: 08:00 UTC is also the Binance funding settlement and the Deribit expiry hour (the GV0CAL-C003 causal-identification blocker class). HK ETF flows are also very small.

### G01-X2 `WEEKEND_BTC_SHARE_PANEL` — `CLOSED_AT_RED_TEAM`

- **Mechanism:** Weekend participants are retail-heavy and rotate into altcoins, lowering BTC's share of spot USDT volume on weekends.
- **Claim:** BTC share of the top-100 spot USDT panel quote volume is lower on Saturday-Sunday than Tuesday-Thursday of the same week.
- **Why closed:** Exchange-specific artifact. Binance zero-fee BTC spot trading (2022-07 to 2023-03) and the 2023 migration of BTC spot liquidity to FDUSD pairs make the BTC share of USDT pairs a measure of fee promotions rather than participant composition. Product relevance is low (the briefing is BTC perp). Acquiring the 18k-object panel is not justified for this card.

### G01-X3 `SESSION_TAKER_SIGN_PROFILE` — `CLOSED_AT_RED_TEAM`

- **Mechanism:** Regional participant populations differ in aggressiveness, so net taker share differs by session.
- **Claim:** Mean net taker share in US-session hours minus Asia-session hours differs from zero.
- **Why closed:** A directional flow claim is INCREMENTAL, not context. A UTC-hour profile does not identify an institutional clock; the only identification (DST shifts) is the D12 template, whose neighbors are forbidden. Funding hours (00/08/16 UTC) confound the session blocks.

### G01-X4 `TAKER_SIGN_PERSISTENCE` — `CLOSED_AT_RED_TEAM`

- **Mechanism:** Order splitting makes the sign of hourly net taker flow persistent.
- **Claim:** P(sign of next-hour net taker share equals this hour's) exceeds 0.5 by a bar.
- **Why closed:** The outcome is not in doubt (long memory of order signs is a known stylized fact), so a test is not informative. H05 and B2-05 governance also deprioritize taker/flow children presented as fresh formulas.

### G01-X5 `SIGNED_SHOCK_RANGE_ASYMMETRY` — `CLOSED_AT_DEDUPE`

- **Mechanism:** Long-liquidation convexity makes ranges after down-shocks wider than after equal-magnitude up-shocks.
- **Claim:** Next-4h range after a down-shock hour exceeds that after an up-shock hour of matched magnitude.
- **Why closed:** Hidden repeat of GV0V03L40-C027 and C003 (inverse-margin and liquidation convexity, down- vs up-shock paths; blocked for confounding control and lookahead), which it does not resolve. Volatility-conditioning neighbor of D2 and D8 (forbidden RV-threshold children; D8 not to be weakened).

### G01-X6 `UNUSUAL_HOUR_PERSISTENCE` — `CLOSED_AT_DEDUPE`

- **Mechanism:** An hour with an extreme same-hour range rank is followed by elevated ranges.
- **Claim:** Next-hour standardized range after a rank >= 0.95 hour exceeds that after ordinary hours.
- **Why closed:** Volatility clustering. The outcome is not in doubt, and the card is an RV-threshold child of D2 (forbidden).

### G01-X7 `EQUITY_OPEX_HOUR` — `CLOSED_AT_RED_TEAM`

- **Mechanism:** US equity monthly options expiry (third Friday) dealer hedging spills into BTC through cross-asset books.
- **Claim:** 15:00-16:00 NY range on the third Friday exceeds the same hour on other Fridays of the month.
- **Why closed:** Rare-event N: one state hour per monthly unit. Under the frozen stress SD the paired MDE is about 0.84 SD, far above the bar, as for R03-A2/A3. The mechanism is also weak a priori.

### G01-X8 `ASIA_LUNCH_PARTICIPATION` — `CLOSED_AT_RED_TEAM`

- **Mechanism:** Asian retail lunch breaks lower participation at fixed UTC hours.
- **Claim:** 02:30-05:00 UTC participation is below adjacent hours.
- **Why closed:** Not identifiable: Asian clocks have no DST, so the claim cannot be separated from a generic UTC hour-of-day profile. Holiday-based identification is the GV0R01-C020 neighbor (data/feasibility blocked).

### G01-X9 `ETF_WEEKEND_GAP_GROWTH` — `CLOSED_AT_RED_TEAM`

- **Mechanism:** ETF-era weekday participation widens the weekday/weekend gap.
- **Claim:** The weekend-minus-weekday range gap widened after 2024-01-11.
- **Why closed:** Leakage from previously exposed outcomes: the idea follows from R03-C1's observed epoch trend (-0.19 in 2020 to -0.65 in 2024) on the same surface. That is post-hoc and a rescue of a closed card.

### G01-X10 `BANK_HOLIDAY_FIAT_RAIL` — `CLOSED_AT_RED_TEAM`

- **Mechanism:** US bank holidays with NYSE open (Columbus Day, Veterans Day) close fiat rails and lower US participation.
- **Claim:** Participation on those days is below matched weekdays.
- **Why closed:** Rare-event N (about 10 days in 2020-2024). Close neighbor of the holiday participant-removal card GV0R01-C020.
